    Stores¶

    Four protocols hold server-side state. Each has an in-memory implementation in the core and a Redis implementation in rn_forge.auth.redis.

    Protocol Holds Redis operation it relies on
    TransactionStore Login transactions between the redirect and the callback. consume returns the transaction to exactly one caller. SET ... EX to save, GETDEL to consume
    SessionStore Login sessions under random IDs. create, get, touch, delete and rotate. SET ... EX, GET, EXPIRE, GETDEL
    ReplayStore Single-use values, such as logout-token jti, and revoked (issuer, sid) pairs. SET key 1 NX EX for record_once, SET ... EX and EXISTS for revoked sid values
    AuthorizationVersions The counters behind AuthorizationContextCache. INCR per account and for the global counter, MGET to read

    A session ends at its idle expiry or at SessionInfo.expires_at, whichever comes first. get does not extend the idle expiry, so a poll cannot keep an idle session alive; touch extends it, never past expires_at. rotate returns a new ID and leaves the old one unreadable. The stores do not check session versions or revoked sid values; the framework binding does that after get.

    from redis import Redis
from rn_forge.auth.redis import RedisSessionStore, RedisTransactionStore

client = Redis.from_url("redis://localhost:6379/0")
sessions = RedisSessionStore(client)
transactions = RedisTransactionStore(client, prefix="myapp-auth:")

session_id = sessions.create(session_info, idle_ttl=timedelta(minutes=30))

    Supported storage¶

    Transactions, replay records and revoked sid values must be shared by every worker, so a store used by more than one process must be backed by shared storage whose operations above are atomic. The in-memory stores (InMemoryTransactionStore, InMemorySessionStore, InMemoryReplayStore and InMemoryAuthorizationVersions) are thread-safe but are not safe across processes; use them in tests and single-process development only. The Redis stores need Redis 6.2 or later (for GETDEL).

    Every Redis store takes a client and a key prefix ("rn-forge-auth:" by default). Expiries are whole seconds, rounded up, and at least one. A session is stored as JSON, and a missing, expired or rotated-away key reads as absent.

    Authorization versions¶

    AuthorizationVersions holds the counters behind AuthorizationContextCache (see Contracts): a version per account and a global version, read together by current(account_id) and raised by bump(account_id) and bump_all(). InMemoryAuthorizationVersions is local to the process, so with several workers a bump reaches only the worker that made it and the others rely on the cache TTL. RedisAuthorizationVersions shares the counters through INCR and MGET.
